finalOwnerStatement: expansion.vscode-web owns this product outcome; semantic algorithms, project resolution, format/lint logic, TypeScript projection and edit transactions stay with their existing producing owners; VSW1+ own vscode-web production under this constitution.
sourceOfTruth: packages/vue-vscode live tree, joined to the VSC0 FeatureOwnershipMatrix and DesktopWebSharedBoundary, the BWH0 platform-host-services inventory and browser-execution-manifest (NativeOnly-in-browser and semantic-host law), and the DX0 feature-exposure-contract operations (hostExecutionClass/browserExecutable); re-derived by tests/vscode-web/VSW0/vsw0.test.mjs
law: The web extension (vscode.dev / github.dev / browser-host mode) is one more consumer of the existing producers: every feature row below keeps its VSC0 owner and host-execution class, binds the DX0 receipt basis for browser-local execution, and reaches native capability only through the explicitly selected companion route. No row forks the desktop extension, gains a second semantic/type/project engine, or copies the whole extension to claim parity.

vocabulary.hostExecutionClass: DX0 host-execution-class.v1 enum (Portable | NativeOnly | ExternalOwner), reused verbatim
vocabulary.receiptBasis: DX0 product-receipt-basis.v1 fields (sourceRevisions, projectConfiguration, engineIdentity, hostIdentity, completenessState)

webDispositionDefinitions.browser-local-route: the feature's web surface executes in the browser extension host over an engine that class already admits in a browser (Portable or ExternalOwner); NativeOnly features may never hold this disposition (dx0ClassPortLaw)
webDispositionDefinitions.gap-pending-class-port: the browser route is planned but is a labelled gap today: the DX0 operation is NativeOnly and not browser-executable, so the route requires a DX0 receiving-owner amendment (class/browserExecutable change or a separately labelled vscode-web Portable operation) before any browser-local claim; until then the surface shows the DX0 unsupported completeness state
webDispositionDefinitions.gap-pending-semantic-host: a labelled gap with two missing producers: the DX0 class-port amendment above and the BWH semantic-host proof (BWH1..BWH6B per the BWH0 browser-execution-manifest portabilityProof); a compiler-WASM build never proves semantic-host portability, so semantic rows may not claim browser-local-route over the wasm surface
webDispositionDefinitions.remote-native-only: the feature keeps executing in the desktop or remote Node extension host; a browser client viewing it is a remote-native session
webDispositionDefinitions.companion-route: native capability reached only through explicitly selected authenticated local-native execution (DX4/DX5) or the remote-native host; never the browser-local receipt
webDispositionDefinitions.static-web-asset: declarative contributions shipped unchanged from either entry

dx0ClassPortLaw.statement: A NativeOnly vscode operation may appear in a browser product only as explicitly selected DX4/DX5 companion execution or as a labelled gap (BWH0 browser-execution-manifest NativeOnly-in-browser rule; DX0-AC2 lineage). A browser-local route for a NativeOnly row requires a DX0 receiving-owner amendment that changes the operation's hostExecutionClass/browserExecutable or adds a separately labelled vscode-web Portable operation; substituting a different engine (the compiler wasm host) does not change the class. No such amendment is recorded today, so every NativeOnly row below carries a gap disposition.

semanticHostLaw.statement: BWH0's compiler-WASM build proves the compiler/session surface only and never proves semantic-host portability (BWH0 browser-execution-manifest portabilityProof; BWH0-AC3). Browser-local semantic routes require the semantic-host proof recorded as receiving-owner amendments before code; until then every semantic row is a labelled gap (gap-pending-semantic-host), never a browser-local-route claim over the compiler wasm surface.

hostModes.definition: vscode.dev / github.dev with the extension's browser entry executing in the local web extension host (web workers). Semantic work rides the BWH wasm host through in-memory platform services only after the BWH semantic-host proof (semanticHostLaw); until then semantic surfaces in this mode are labelled gaps, never compiler-wasm parity claims.
VS Code desktop with the extension's main entry executing in the local Node extension host. This is the only shipped mode today.

Codespaces / SSH / WSL / tunnel remote workspace: the main entry executes in the remote Node extension host. A browser client viewing this workspace is a remote-native session, never browser-local parity.
hostModes.deliveryOwner: expansion.vscode-product (VSC train; the Node bundle runs unchanged remotely)

browserLocalReceipt.sourceRevisions: the virtual-workspace file revisions synchronized through the web VFS (VSW2); stale or wrong-handle results are rejected before display
browserLocalReceipt.projectConfiguration: the browser project profile: in-memory workspace identity, framework profile and configuration facts carried by the web host; no ambient filesystem reads exist in the browser closure
browserLocalReceipt.engineIdentity: the row's webEngine: the Verter compiler WASM build, the pinned browser TypeScript worker (ExternalOwner), or the explicitly selected companion engine with its exact version
browserLocalReceipt.hostIdentity: browser runtime plus WASM build selector (DX0 product-receipt-basis wasm-build-selector substrate); remote-native-only and companion-route rows override this field and may not claim it
browserLocalReceipt.completenessState: DX0 completenessStates; complete-empty is a successful empty answer; partial, pending, unsupported, ambiguous, failed, cancelled and stale are distinct and never published as complete

rules: every VSC0 feature id has exactly one row here with a webDisposition from this vocabulary; a new desktop feature without a row is drift, not implicit coverage

a NativeOnly row is never browser-local-route or static-web-asset: it is gap-pending-class-port, gap-pending-semantic-host (when its engine is the wasm semantic surface), companion-route or remote-native-only, per dx0ClassPortLaw and semanticHostLaw; a gap disposition exists only on a NativeOnly row

a row that names its planned route (browser-local-route or either gap disposition) names its routeOwner in the VSW train and its webEngine; a remote-native-only or companion-route row must override hostIdentityOverride and may not claim the browserLocalReceipt hostIdentity
webDisposition changes are producer-owned ports with their own evidence, never relabels (VSC0 no-class-change-by-moving-code)
bwhServices cited by a row must exist in the BWH0 platform-host-services inventory

a row citing a live desktop-tier DesktopWebSharedBoundary module lists it in desktopTierModules and states its desktopTierRoute (VSW1 conversion or desktop-by-design); no row claims host-neutral readiness for a desktop-tier module

the web entry is placed at packages/vue-vscode/src/browser with host-neutral modules at packages/vue-vscode/src/shared and its suite at packages/vue-vscode/e2e/web (VSW1+ own those directories; VSW0 adds none of them)
acBasisDownstreamTestOwner: VSW1 owns the browser-entrypoint build admission and shared-code module-load runtime checks; VSW5 owns packaging, offline and browser-matrix qualification on real artifacts
acResourceRationale: VSW0 touches no hot paths and no UI: 0 production LOC across 0 files, so the WSP equal-work corpus and client-paint obligations do not apply here; real-client claims bind to VSW5
acExposureRegistration: DX1 owns the exposure-descriptor registration schema; no new operation is promoted by this contract node
